extracted.intended_audience: Korean patent examiners (and patent applicants/practitioners responding to KIPO notices)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examiners on when and how to issue notices/decisions of grounds for rejection (final vs non-final), how to examine claim-by-claim, and how to format and cite supporting prior art in written notices and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to reject when amended claim identical to previously-notified rejected claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amended claim is identical to the other claim to which a ground of rejection was notified, a decision to reject shall be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amended claim duplicates a claim already notified as containing a ground of rejection, the examiner must make a decision to reject that amended claim (examples in the manual illustrate identical/newly added claims identical to previously-notified indefinite claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-final rejection — scope and triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'non-final rejection' may be issued regardless of voluntary amendments if it is the first notice since the start of examination, where an unamended portion of the specification includes a ground for rejection, or where the ground arises from the description/claims before amendment rather than from the amendment itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (1) issuing novelty/inventive-step rejection based on pre-amendment claim content even after the claim was amended; (2) notifying additional inventions within a single claim in stages — subsequent notifications are non-final; (3) ex-officio re-examination and remanded applications have special rules resulting in non-final notices in certain circumstances. Examiner should issue non-final when grounds are not necessitated by amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection necessitated by amendment — definition and prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: A final rejection necessitated by amendment is issued where the ground for rejection arises from amendments made in response to a previously issued notice of rejection; prerequisites include that written amendments were submitted and a new ground of rejection was incurred because of the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific examples: (1) amendments adding new matter or exceeding scope (divisional/converted); (2) amendments that introduce elements causing lack of novelty or inventive step (requiring new prior art search); (3) newly added claims or claims changed equivalent to new additions that contain novelty/inventive-step problems. If an amended claim equals another claim never notified for rejection, issue non-final instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rule — issue non-final unless all grounds qualify as final
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner rediscovers grounds for rejection upon re-examination, the examiner shall issue a non-final rejection unless all of the grounds fall under 'final rejection necessitated by the amendment.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the applicant's opportunity to amend; only use final rejection when every ground meets the 'necessitated by amendment' standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection rule — when in doubt issue non-final
rubrics_metrics.description: Where uncertainty pertains to the selection between final and non-final rejection, an examiner shall issue the non-final rejection so that the applicant’s opportunity of amendment may not be unreasonably limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When it's unclear whether the ground was created by amendment, favor non-final notices to avoid unduly restricting applicant remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of claim-by-claim examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner examines an application on a claim-by-claim basis to ensure that when notifying grounds of rejection for multi-claim applications, specific claims and reasons are identified so applicants can identify which claims are remediable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The aim is to avoid vague, application-level rejections that make it hard for applicants to know what to amend or delete to preserve patentable subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice component: 'Claims to be Examined'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Claims to be Examined' stipulates the number (and identity) of claims to be examined as of the date the written notice is prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the claims subject to examination at that moment — this frames which claims are evaluated and which are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice component: 'Relevant Provisions regarding Grounds for Rejection'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Relevant Provisions regarding Grounds for Rejection' specifies claims containing the grounds for rejection and the relevant statutory provisions; if the ground is not directly related to claims, state the matters containing the ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment adds new matter or exceeds scope in a divisional/converted application, those newly added or excluded matters must be stated as grounds for rejection here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice component: 'Patentable Claim' (what to list)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Patentable Claim' enumerates all claims that are not identified as grounds for rejection at the time of notice, but it is not an examiner's final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: do not list claims as patentable if special circumstances make assessment impossible at the time, if a claim's patentability depends on other grounds, or if a new ground is later discovered. Explain reasons in 'Considerations of Amendment' when omitting claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notice component: 'Specific Grounds for Rejection' — specificity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Specific Grounds for Rejection' must set out more specific reasons for the matters notified as grounds for rejection so applicants can respond effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: (①) state grounds per claim (can group to avoid redundancy); ② indicate which parts of prior art are used in comparison and select closest prior art; ③ specify prior art references and describe differences and inventive-step assessment in an understandable way; ④ separate grounds for independent and dependent claims and include dependent-claim grounds; ⑤ prepare (when helpful) a component comparison table mapping claimed features to prior-art features and supply examiner assessment and common general knowledge reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of component comparison table
rubrics_metrics.description: When comparing claims and prior art, an examiner may prepare a component comparison table to show relations between distinguishing claimed components and corresponding prior-art features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The table may include locations in cited documents and can include the examiner's judgment in or below the table; examples are provided showing mapping of A/B/C features and narrative conclusions regarding obviousness/combination of references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations of Amendment — content and caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Considerations of Amendment' states matters that are not grounds for rejection but are useful for an applicant's response (e.g., examiner opinions about the description, reasons for not listing certain claims as patentable, and other amendment considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: if the examiner intends to use contents of 'Considerations of Amendment' as grounds for rejection later, they must make notice of the ground for rejection again (i.e., cannot convert consideration into a ground without re-notification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of written decision to reject — structure
rubrics_metrics.description: A written decision to reject is prepared similarly to a written notice of grounds for rejection, except entries reflect 'matters where the ground for rejection is not overcome' and relevant statutory provisions for those matters; sections include Claims to be Examined, Relevant Provisions for Matters Where Grounds Not Overcome, Patentable Claims, Grounds for Decision to Reject, and Considerations in Amendment Submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no written argument or amendment was submitted in response to prior notice, an examiner may omit separate 'Examination Results' and 'Rationale for Decision to Reject' sections. Newly added claims identical to previously-notified rejected claims are considered an opportunity to have argued and are listed as matters where rejection grounds are not overcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for Decision to Reject — level of explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Grounds for Decision to Reject' must state specific rationale for grounds not overcome and explain why applicant's amendments or arguments do not overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When both written arguments and amendments are submitted, the examiner must explain why the amendment fails and why arguments are denied. For claims without practical amendments or dependent claims without direct amendment, a short statement that the previously-notified ground is not overcome may suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in Amendment Submission (decision context)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Considerations in Amendment Submission' lists issues not themselves grounds for rejection but that applicants should consider when submitting further amendments or requests for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include noting that additional grounds may arise from added claims or amendments and that such matters can be provided in 'Considerations' to inform subsequent prosecution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim instruction: handling description deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the description has deficiencies, claims that do not themselves contain grounds for rejection may be classified under 'Patentable Claims' unless exceptional circumstances make patentability assessment impossible at notice time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a claim is related to a notified description deficiency or examiner believes amendment cannot remedy the deficiency, the examiner should explain why the claim is not included as patentable in 'Considerations of Amendment'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim instruction: citing claims that reference other claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a claim cites another claim that violates Article 42(4), the examiner must assess whether the citing claim continues to have the same ground; if so, state that the citing claim has the same ground for rejection as the cited claim. If the cited claim only violates the manner of describing claims (Article 42(8)), only the cited claim is stated to have that ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between substantive deficiencies carried through claim dependency and mere form/manner-of-description defects limited to the cited claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim instruction: multiple invention groups and unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application involves two or more groups of inventions, the examiner normally considers patentability for inventions in at least one group; when pointing out lack of unity, indicate claims in another group rather than the group already evaluated for novelty/inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims without grounds among the evaluated group may be included in 'Patentable Claims'; if the examiner did not perform patentability tests for some groups, note this in 'Considerations of Amendment' and do not include those claims in 'Patentable Claims'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of prior art information must comply with WIPO ST.14
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing grounds for rejection related to prior-art technical subject matter, the examiner shall cite supporting documents and disclose information on prior art documents in accordance with WIPO Standard ST.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow WIPO ST.14 for methods not specified in this section; ensures consistent, internationally-understood citation practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing patent documents supporting a ground for rejection, the cited patent documents shall be clearly stated in the order of publishing country (can be omitted if Korea), title of patent documents, document number (laid-open number), and publication date (public disclosure date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title and document number are stated as in the patent documents. Examples are provided for Korea, US, Japan, UK, Germany, and international publications. For abstracts, include classification notation in parentheses as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: When citing patent docs indicate which parts are used (pages/drawings)
rubrics_metrics.description: When patent documents are cited for grounds of rejection, the examiner shall clearly state which part of the documents are used for citation by using page or drawing numbers in parentheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show appending '(No. of page and drawing)' or indicating a figure name/number after the citation; improves clarity about what portion of the document the examiner relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for non-patent documents (periodicals and books)
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing non-patent publications, use the order: Name of Author, Title of Thesis, Title of Publication. Location of Publication: Publisher. Publication Date, Number of Volumes, Number of Issues, Page No.; for books use analogous ordering and formatting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed punctuation and formatting rules: use periods and colons as specified, do not abbreviate publication titles generally, 'Vol. oo, No. oo' for English publications, omit location for Korean publications, use 'pp.' for page ranges, italicize publication/book titles, explain handling of missing dates or unclear publication data, and include page/drawing numbers when citing a part of a publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format for electronic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing electronic documents (CD-ROM, internet, online DB), the examiner shall state general information of the cited documents along with the type of search medium (in braces), the search date (in braces after publication date), and the search site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance: include medium type, date the examiner accessed the document, and the site used so the applicant can locate the cited electronic reference.
